detail: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cleanup_old_pending_invites() RETURNS INTEGER, LANGUAGE plpgsql, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = public. Behavior: DELETE FROM public.pending_user_invites WHERE created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'; captures ROW_COUNT into deleted_count; then INSERT INTO public.activity_logs (action, details, user_email) VALUES ('cleanup_pending_invites', format('Automatically cleaned up %s old pending invites', deleted_count), 'system'); returns deleted_count. COMMENT ON FUNCTION explains it removes pending invites older than 30 days to reduce email-harvesting exposure; callable manually by admins or via pg_cron.
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.cleanup_old_pending_invites() TO authenticated. Note: granted to all authenticated users, not just admins (comment says 'admins will use this').
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pending_invites_created_at ON public.pending_user_invites(created_at). For efficient cleanup queries.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cleanup_activity_logs() RETURNS trigger, LANGUAGE plpgsql, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = 'public'. Behavior: DELETE FROM public.activity_logs WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM public.activity_logs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20); RETURN NEW. Keeps only the 20 most recent activity_logs rows.

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trigger_cleanup_activity_logs ON public.activity_logs; then CREATE TRIGGER trigger_cleanup_activity_logs AFTER INSERT ON public.activity_logs FOR EACH STATEMENT EXECUTE FUNCTION public.cleanup_activity_logs(). Every insert into activity_logs trims the table to the latest 20 rows.

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user() RETURNS TRIGGER, LANGUAGE plpgsql, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = public. Behavior: INSERT INTO public.profiles (id, email, full_name) VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.email, COALESCE(NEW.raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name', '')); then INSERT INTO public.user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES (NEW.id, CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM auth.users) = 1 THEN 'Admin'::app_role ELSE 'Admin'::app_role END). Both CASE branches yield 'Admin' — EVERY new signup is assigned the Admin role (inline comment says to change ELSE branch to 'Client'/'Contractor' for default role).
DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS on_auth_user_created ON auth.users; then CREATE TRIGGER on_auth_user_created AFTER INSERT ON auth.users FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.handle_new_user().
